question: How do they match words before reordering them?

evidence: We use the CFILT-preorder system for reordering English sentences to match the Indian language word order. It contains two re-ordering systems: (1) generic rules that apply to all Indian languages BIBREF17 , and (2) hindi-tuned rules which improve the generic rules by incorporating improvements found through an error analysis of English-Hindi reordering BIBREF28 . These Hindi-tuned rules have been found to improve reordering for many English to Indian language pairs BIBREF29 .

title: Addressing word-order Divergence in Multilingual Neural Machine Translation for extremely Low Resource Languages
answer_short: They match words before reordering them by pre-ordering the assisting language sentences to match the word order of the source language.
answer_rationale: The document explains that to address word order divergence, the assisting language sentences (e.g., English) are pre-ordered to match the word order of the source language (e.g., SOV for Bengali). This pre-ordering ensures that the encoder generates consistent contextual representations, which helps the attention network and decoder transfer knowledge effectively. The CFILT-preorder system is used for this purpose, applying generic and language-tuned rules to reorder sentences.
